newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech import surcharge must come from parliament-P.
newsitem.headline: Czech import surcharge must come from parliament-P.

text.p: The Czech parliament must approve any imposition of an import surcharge, as it cannot come solely from the government, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

"It is not possible to impose an import surcharge in the Czech Republic by a government decision, but only by a law ...which makes it, from the point of view of the April 16 (economic development) package, an absolutely uninteresting measure, if only from the timing point of view," Klaus told a news conference.
The Czech government has been debating steps to stem the growth of both a worsening trade deficit and a growing budget deficit, and has said it hoped to announce a package measures on April 16.

Agrigiculture Minister Josef Lux has called for an import surcharge to help take pressure off the trade deficit which has pushed the current account deficit to more than eight percent of gross domestic product.
No concrete decisions were announced after the cabinet meeting, held in the country chateau of Kolodeje east of Prague.
Klaus and other senior ministers were expected to meet later today in Kolodeje with Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky.
